name: ColecoVision
description: Coleco's 1982 console brought near arcade-quality graphics home and launched with a strong Donkey Kong port. It used off-the-shelf chips also found in MSX computers and the Sega SG-1000, and its expansion modules even let it play Atari 2600 games.
curiosities: Donkey Kong was bundled with the console.
Expansion Module #1 let it play Atari 2600 cartridges, prompting a lawsuit from Atari.
Expansion Module #3 turned it into the Coleco Adam computer.
Its controllers had a 12-button keypad that took game-specific overlays.
story: Coleco, a maker of toys and pools, launched the ColecoVision in August 1982 with a near-perfect port of Nintendo's Donkey Kong bundled with it.

It gave home players something close to the arcade, and an adapter even played Atari 2600 cartridges. Zaxxon, Venture, Lady Bug and Mr. Do! followed. It sold about two million units in its first eighteen months.
The crash of 1983 and Coleco's Adam computer, which began as an add-on for it, ended it by 1985; homebrew games have kept coming.
